summary: The prepared source already contains the post-report Run:AI ownership fix from upstream PR #32896. Deterministic regression and gfx950 checks verify the reported reusable-buffer corruption mechanism is prevented in the shared GLM/DeepSeek loader paths; no duplicate production change was made.

tests.what_was_measured: 11 registered loader tests passed, including a deterministic control that reads an overwritten reusable buffer and a marked Run:AI case that preserves the pre-reuse value.

On gfx950, fused block-FP8 DSA-indexer loading matched an independent dequantized reference with max_abs_error=0.0 for marked tensors in weight-first and scale-first order; both unmarked reuse controls had max_abs_error=1.0.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the fused DSA-indexer ownership check; raw log: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-03a3dcef4d7e/evidence/gpu_runai_indexer_ownership.log

remaining_limitations: The assigned worker has one AMD gfx950 GPU, not the reported eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs, so TP8, CUDA/TRT-LLM, full-model generation, semantic accuracy, and tool-call behavior remain unverified.
The result verifies the exact reusable-buffer ownership mechanism and relevant current loader paths; it does not claim a full serving reproduction.
